note: The activities a business performs, as Naive data (EE-164). An activity is a unit of work (APQC level 4) written as an O*NET task statement and filed under an APQC level 2 process group from tools.json, cross-industry or for one NAICS industry. An activity may be scored on the scales below. A score is one rater's judgment, and every scored activity names who rated it, when and on what basis. This catalog is version 0.x and unevaluated: no score has been compared with an outcome. A score never decides anything: the most it may do is propose an open decision for a person, and nothing reads scores yet. The list of activities is empty until it is seeded. Checked by packages/naive/src/checks/check-activities.ts.

scales.means: How far legal, professional or social institutions restrict the activity, from R0 (no professional or statutory barrier) to R4, on the CDR taxonomy's regulatory restrictions axis
How much physical deployment or embodiment the activity needs, from D0 (no physical interaction) to D4, on the CDR taxonomy's deployment difficulty axis
The level of reasoning and judgment the activity requires, from C0 to C4, on the CDR taxonomy's cognitive complexity axis

Where checking the activity's result falls, from 1 (rare experts who disagree, no inspectable artifact) to 10 (a fully deterministic programmatic check), on the RL feasibility index's verification method dimension
How important the activity is to the work, from 1 (not important) to 5 (extremely important), as O*NET rates a task's importance
The percent of practitioners who perform the activity, as O*NET's relevance scale counts the incumbents who report a task
How often the activity is performed, from 1 (yearly or less) to 7 (hourly or more), on O*NET's seven frequency categories
